svg.title: The right-sized stack: Graviton5 at half the size in three tiers
svg.desc: AWS architecture diagram: load generators, an internet gateway and an Application Load Balancer, the web, API and system node groups of an Amazon EKS cluster in two Availability Zones, an Aurora MySQL writer and reader, and the delivery pipeline.
svg.text: The right-sized stack: Graviton5 at half the size in three tiers
The same network, cluster, load balancer and database volume. A green bar marks what changed from the baseline.
Load generators: Distributed Load Testing on AWS
k6 on AWS Fargate at a fixed arrival rate: 31% page requests, 69% direct API calls
/api/* to API pods, the rest to web pods
Solid arrows: page requests (31%); each rendered page makes one main call to the API. Dashed arrows: direct API calls (69%).
Every query goes to the Aurora writer. The three node groups each span both zones.
Every change is a commit that AWS CodePipeline applies, in six steps:
